input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The separator selection negates any_prefix_is_slash, picking ' / ' exactly when an option spelling already starts with a slash and '; ' otherwise.
- failure path: An option declared as --shout/--no-shout renders in --help as '--shout; --no-shout', and a Windows-style /debug;/no-debug option renders as '/debug / /no-debug', where the slash separator is indistinguishable from the slash prefix of the names.

Reviewer finding
- description: The separator condition was inverted when moving the join into get_help_spec: it now uses "; " when any_prefix_is_slash is false and " / " when it is true, the opposite of the original code.
- rationale: Trigger: any option with no slash prefix, such as --verbose with -v, reaches this join. Originally it rendered as "-v / --verbose"; with the inverted condition it renders as "-v; --verbose". Options that do use slash prefixes get the wrong separator too. Mechanism: the ternary branches are swapped relative to the original `if any_prefix_is_slash else`. Impact: every option's help left column in the rendered --help output changes, which is a user-visible regression.
critique: The finding pinpoints the same inverted any_prefix_is_slash condition in the separator selection. It describes the same failure: non-slash options get '; ' instead of ' / ', and slash-prefixed options get the wrong separator.
